cumleler: Can an audiogram tell a cochlear loss from a retrocochlear one?
A pure-tone audiogram alone cannot separate cochlear and retrocochlear loss.
First red flag: asymmetric loss unexplained by noise or age.
One-sided tinnitus, especially new or worsening, also needs attention.
A speech score too low for the hearing loss is another clue.
The audiologist then reports the findings and refers to a physician.
